Subject: Performance SLO follow-up: context window, tokens & latency impact

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for a great call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope a short proof run: 

Summary from our discussion:
- Target p95 latency: 300ms for interactive queries (typical prompt sizes under ~1k input tokens).
- Streaming required: want partial answer token-by-token to start showing results within <200ms if possible.
- Concurrency: estimate 150-250 concurrent active users at peak, with bursts up to ~400 for batch jobs.
- Context window: your retrieval layer will surface ~40k tokens of context for some workflows (customer history + documents). We discussed that long context will affect completion latency.
- Desired SLA: 99.9% uptime, monthly latency report and token cost breakdown.

Action items I promised: 
1) Share a short performance matrix that contrasts model/context window choices vs expected latency and token-cost (attached).
2) Rishi will outline how context length affects time-to-first-token and per-token cost and propose mitigations.
3) Align on a small live perf run: can we schedule a 60-min live test next week where we run your typical retrieval-to-generation path against a dedicated instance?

Attachments: redwood-performance-matrix.pdf, SLO template.

If the above matches your notes, can you confirm which of these three flows is highest priority for the pilot (A: short chat, B: RAG with 8-16k context, C: long-history RAG with 40k+ context)?

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up: context window, tokens & latency impact

Thanks for the recap, Marissa — adding technical context to Samir's questions. I'll keep this high-level but with actionable numbers we can test in a pilot.

1) Context window impact (short answers):
- Time-to-first-byte (TTFB): primarily driven by model forward pass for the first generated token. If you provide a 40k-token prefix, the initial TTFB increases because the model needs to process the full prefix once (KV cache warmup happens, but the prefix still needs to be encoded). In practice, TTFB for autoregressive models with a ~40k prefix can be 2-5x higher than for a 1k prefix depending on model size and kernel optimizations. Expect p95 TTFB around 300-700ms on GPU-optimized long-context configs for 40k inputs (model dependent).

- Per-token generation latency: once the KV cache is populated, per-token generation cost depends on model size and kernel efficiency; it grows sub-linearly with prefix length because the heavy cost per step is the generation step (with cached keys). So long prefixes mainly hurt initial latency more than per-token throughput.

- Attention complexity: many long-context solutions (sliding window, chunked attention, memory layers) reduce the quadratic costs, but they can change output quality/behavior- worth validating on your prompts.

2) Streaming behavior:
- Streaming (server-sent events / chunked responses) reduces perceived latency: you can see first tokens as soon as TTFB completes. This improves user experience even if full completion occurs later.
- For long-context flows we prioritize time-to-first-token; Redwood supports partial streaming and progressive flushing so the UI can display partial answers while the model continues.

3) Concurrency/throughput guidance:
- Example: 70B-class model on a recent A100/V100-equivalent VM with optimized kernels can serve ~6-12 tokens/sec per GPU at latency-focused config; batch and throughput configs increase tokens/sec but at higher TTFB variance.
- With 250 concurrent users at 1 request/20s (~12 requests/min), if average completion is 2s and average generated tokens per request is 150, you should target a Dedicated pool sized for ~3-4 GPUs for latency SLAs (ballpark). We'll run a live perf test to produce precise numbers.

4) Mitigations and recommendations before the pilot:
- Reduce prefix size by summarizing or retrieving top-k compressed context snippets.
- Use a model variant with long-context kernels (we have 32k/65k-optimized variants) and quantized runtime (int8/4) to lower latency and cost.
- Enable streaming and early-flush of partial answers in the UI.
- For absolute 300ms p95 on 1k prompts, use a latency-optimized instance profile and smaller model family (e.g., 13B-34B) if quality allows; reserve larger models for high-quality long-context flows.

Next steps: I can run a short benchmark (your sample prompts + 1k/16k/40k contexts, 1-4 concurrent request profiles, and burst patterns). Can we get a small representative dataset (50-100 prompts with expected context sizes)?

- Rishi
Staff SE, Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi — that's exactly the level of detail we needed.

For the pilot we'll prioritize flow B (RAG with 8-16k context) and also run a smaller set of tests for flow C (40k) to validate worst-case behavior. We'll send a representative set of ~60 prompts across both buckets by EOD Friday.

A few clarifications:
- For the 8-16k bucket, target p95 of 350ms TTFB is acceptable if streaming can show first tokens within ~200ms.
- For the 40k tests we accept higher TTFB (up to 800ms p95) as long as partial streaming starts earlier and overall completion for 150 tokens remains reasonable.

Procurement: looping in Alyssa Green (cc) - she will coordinate contracting for Dedicated capacity if the pilot numbers align. Alyssa, do you have a preferred NDA/PO flow?
